user.title: Add a monitored host
user.description: One entry per host. Nothing is installed on the host and no agent has to be running on it — every reading is taken over SSH. The hostname is read from the host itself using the SSH credential below; type it in for a host that is deliberately powered down.

data_description.ssh_user: A read-only account is enough for monitoring — every value collected on a schedule comes from a world-readable file or an unprivileged query. Passwordless sudo is needed only if you later turn on remote patching and reboot for this host, and that option probes for it before it will accept.
data_description.offline_expected: Set for a host that is deliberately powered down. It will be named and dispositioned rather than reported as a fault, and no polling is attempted.

error.cannot_connect: Could not read the hostname over SSH. Check the address, that the account exists on that host, and that its public key is in the account's authorized_keys. If the host is deliberately powered down, tick 'Intentionally offline' and supply the hostname.
error.hostname_required_offline: An intentionally-offline host cannot be probed for its name — enter it manually.

init.title: Linux Monitor options

data_description.offline_expected: When set, the host is not polled and its health reports OK rather than a fault.
data_description.allow_install: Off by default. Turning it on adds an Install button for this host in Home Assistant's Updates panel, puts it in the update-all path there, and creates a Reboot host button. Both need passwordless sudo for this entry's SSH account, which is checked over that exact account and key before the setting is saved.

init.description: Remote patching runs apt-get upgrade — never full-upgrade, which can remove packages — and reboots the host only if apt exits 0.

error.no_sudo: This host's SSH account cannot run sudo without a password, or the host could not be reached to ask. Remote patching was NOT enabled — an unreachable host is not a yes. Grant passwordless sudo to that account on the host, or leave the option off and patch it by hand.
